messages:
Sam K: quick question / sanity check about generate endpoint behavior when using streaming + stop sequences + logprobs. I hit a case in PR #842 where streaming chunks after a stop never include logprobs, but non-streaming response does. sample curl below. Anyone seen this? :eyes:

Sam K: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-7b","prompt":"List steps","stop":["\n\n"],"max_tokens":50,"temperature":0.0,"top_p":1.0,"logprobs":5,"stream":true}'
```

Mariana P: I can repro. When stream: true, the runtime emits token events until a stop is matched, then emits a final event but logprobs are null in that final chunk. Non-stream aggregates and returns logprobs for tokens up to the stop. Seems like we drop the per-token logprob payload when we short-circuit on stop.

Kevin L: that's because we optimize away the KV cache emission for the last partial batch. For backcompat I'd prefer we include final token logprobs whenever requested (even if stop ended early). Changing that should be low-risk but touches the emitter.

Oli: note edge with temperature/top_p interplay: at temp=0 or top_p=0 behavior is deterministic; we still sample but deterministic sampling can change token boundaries vs stop detection order in streaming. CI had a flaky test where stop matched only after one extra token when top_p=0. :thinking:

Jess: Is this explicitly defined in the API contract? If not, we should add a short paragraph that: (a) streaming will attempt to include token-level logprobs for all emitted tokens including final stop tokens when logprobs requested; (b) max_tokens is an upper bound on generated tokens and stop can terminate earlier; (c) if logprobs unavailable for any reason, fields will be null and a warning field will be set.

Kevin L: good wording. I'll draft a tiny contract patch and add a compatibility note. Also need to clarify whether max_tokens counts tokens after the stop (it does not — stops end generation early). Add an explicit example.

Mariana P: also confirm SDKs: old JS SDK v0.9 still assumes last chunk may have null logprobs. We need a migration note for users upgrading to runtime that fixes this (might change streaming payload shape).

qa-bot: created test: generate_stream_stop_logprobs_case in our e2e suite and added to flaky suppression list for now. Ticket: QA-1297.

deploy-bot: canary deployed rwd-runtime v3.7.2 to staging with the emitter fix toggled off (flag: include_final_logprobs=false).

Sam K: thanks. I'll open PR with acceptance tests and a small changelog blurb. cc @Kevin L @Mariana P for review. planning to ship the contract change + runtime toggle in next minor release. :thumbsup:

Oli: one more nit — we should document how logprobs are reported when stop token consumes multiple characters (multi-byte) vs single token. Might affect frontends. I'll add a short note to the RFC.

Kevin L: noted. Sam, assign PR to me and Oli. I'll aim to review within 24h.

Sam K: done — PR #856 opened with test and example in docs. pinging for review when you have a moment.

Jess: thanks — will update SDK issue tracker with the migration note.

Mariana P: marking this P1 for Dedicated customers due to observed production regressions.

Sam K: great, thanks everyone.
